---
# No title:/author: — the letterhead pulled in below IS the heading, and it
# must be identical to the cover letter's.
#
# Body font: 12pt in .docx (Word's default), 11pt in .pdf. Both sit inside
# the required 10-12pt range. Section headings come out larger than body
# text in both formats, which is the intended contrast.
format:
  docx:
    number-sections: false
  pdf:
    documentclass: article
    geometry: margin=0.75in
    fontsize: 11pt
    mainfont: Times New Roman
    linestretch: 1
    indent: false
    colorlinks: false
    number-sections: false
---

RULES THAT APPLY TO EVERY SECTION BELOW — read once, then fill in.

ORDER is fixed by the chronological-resume structure the instructor
specified: identifying info, education, employment, skills, activities.
Reverse chronological WITHIN each section (most recent entry first).

NO FIRST-PERSON PRONOUNS anywhere. No "I," "me," "my," "us." Bullets start
with a verb, not a subject.

PARALLEL STRUCTURE. Within one entry, every bullet takes the same
grammatical shape. Past roles use past tense throughout; your current role
uses present tense throughout. Do not mix.

ACTION VERBS, NOT REPEATED. Each bullet opens with a different strong verb.
Verbs that fit this BD role: Analyzed, Researched, Sourced, Qualified,
Built, Negotiated, Coordinated, Presented, Delivered, Streamlined,
Increased, Secured, Forecasted, Mapped. Do not open three bullets with
"Managed."

Development Intern ad. Pull its language in where it is HONESTLY true of
your experience: market research, commercialization strategy, pipeline
management, lead qualification, partnerships, market intelligence,
cross-functional collaboration, industry trends.

PUNCTUATION CONSISTENCY. Pick one rule for bullet endings — periods on all
of them, or periods on none — and hold it across the whole document.

ONE PAGE. If it spills onto page two, cut bullets rather than shrinking the
font below 10pt or narrowing the margins further. Check there is no empty
trailing page before submitting.

NO REFERENCES SECTION, and no "References available upon request."

<!-- CURRENT ROLE — present tense throughout. Every other entry below is

**Software Consultant**\
Invent Labs — Lubbock, Texas\
*July 2026 – Present*

- Advises several software companies on technical and commercial growth strategy, spanning platform architecture decisions and go-to-market positioning.
- Collaborates with established engineering teams to help them adopt new industry trends such as AI native development.
- Scopes and negotiates client engagements end to end, from initial discovery through signed statement of work.
- Identifies client pain points during discovery conversations and translates them into prioritized technical solutions.

**Head of Engineering**\
Palpabl — Lubbock, Texas\
*September 2025 – July 2026*

- Owned the full product lifecycle of a cloud-native, multi-tenant SaaS platform, from concept origination through production-ready MVP delivery and go-to-market positioning.
- Drove the self-service commercialization strategy, including subscription infrastructure, storefront, and automated customer onboarding.
- Directed a team of 5 engineers and delivered the platform to go-live readiness within six months of active development.
- Worked with marketing and product teams to get company alignment and cross-cut non technical stakeholder requirements into positive technical outcomes.
- Prospected and qualified Palpabl's first paying customer and lead them through the onboarding process establishing critical go to market patterns for follow on sales associates.

**Software Engineer**\
Mandry Technology — Lubbock, Texas\
*July 2024 – October 2025*

- Authored the go-to-market brief establishing a $2–5 billion total addressable market and the platform's initial pricing model, presented for executive review, later approved.
- Secured three design-partner commitments by qualifying prospective accounts and leading solution discussions.
- Delivered a full-stack SaaS alpha in eleven months, building the application, cloud infrastructure, and automated release pipeline.
